AST SpaceMobile Sinks 8% as New Offering Filing Revives Dilution Fears ©@Seasonal via Canva, @Oleksii Mach via Canva
Key Takeaways

AST SpaceMobile fell 8% today after a new filing, its second in two days, pointed to another securities sale.

Selling stock near a 52-week low is the costliest way to fund the build-out.

The diluted share count rose from 200 million to 300 million between late 2024 and the third quarter of 2026.

AT&T and Vodafone need the satellites funded, and a launch date for BlueBirds 14 to 16 is the next test.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) sank 8% today on a filing that points to more dilution. The news reaches AT&T (T:NYSE) and Vodafone (VOD) too, which sell AST's coverage to their subscribers and own stakes in the company.

On Tuesday morning, a prospectus supplement covered 10 million Class A shares AST issued to Firefly Aerospace. After Tuesday's close, an 8-K added a legal opinion, usually a sign of a securities sale. Then, before today's open, AST filed a new supplement covering [THE OFFERING'S TYPE AND SIZE, FROM THE 424B5].

AT&T generated $5.0 billion of free cash flow in the third quarter, so a smaller AST stake barely registers. A stalled constellation would matter far more now that SpaceX is buying spectrum for phone service of its own. Vodafone, AST's partner in a European satellite venture, just raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted free cash flow guidance to €2.8 billion to €3.0 billion.

The bill keeps growing

Free cash flow came to about -$1.8 billion over the last four quarters, against $3.2 billion of cash. Analysts expect free cash flow to stay negative through 2028, while revenue climbs from $70.9 million in 2025 to $1.65 billion:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

The 2027 estimate has already fallen to $586 million, from $748 million at the end of June.

TIKR tracks 13 analysts on AST SpaceMobile. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AST SpaceMobile, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AST SpaceMobile's Analyst Ratings

Selling low costs more shares

The share count has grown by half in under two years:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): diluted shares outstanding, millions of shares, last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)

The count flattened in 2026 as AST leaned on convertible notes, including July's $1.15 billion, which convert at about $80 a share. At today's price, a new share brings in about a third of that. Forward price/sales was 21x at the last close, against a five-year average of 60x:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's drop takes it lower still, to about 19x. Another raise was always coming, and I'd expect AST to keep selling stock until launches pick up. BlueBirds 14 to 16 still don't have a launch date, and the target for about 45 satellites has slipped to mid-2027. Fourth-quarter results early next year need a firm launch schedule and 2026 revenue inside the $150 million to $200 million guidance.

Key Takeaways

Contour Asset Management, which manages $5.92 billion, sold all of its AT&T, Rocket Companies and Formula One Group shares in the third quarter, according to its latest 13F.

AT&T was the biggest of the three exits, at 5.9% of Contour's 13F stocks on June 30.

Rocket's falling price targets support the sale. Formula One Group had a record quarter, but it trades at about 54x forward earnings.

The numbers argue hardest against the AT&T sale, at about 9x forward earnings, though SpaceX's push into wireless is a real risk.

Contour Asset Management just sold three of its biggest positions. Its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16, shows that the firm sold every share it held of AT&T (T:NYSE), Rocket Companies (RKT:NYSE) and Formula One Group (FWON-K:NASDAQ).

These weren't small bets

Contour manages $5.92 billion in all, and its 13F held $4.16 billion of US stocks across 29 positions on Sept. 30. On June 30, AT&T made up 6% of its 13F stocks, Rocket 5.6% and Formula One Group 3.8%. Contour was buying too: it more than doubled its Trimble shares and nearly doubled its Iron Mountain stake, which made them its No. 2 and No. 3 holdings. A 13F shows only what a fund held on the last day of the quarter, so we can't know when Contour sold or what price it got.

AT&T has a SpaceX problem and a cheap price

Contour held 12.08 million AT&T shares, worth $250 million, on June 30. The stock is up 8% from its June 30 price, but it still sits 24% below its 52-week high.

The worry is SpaceX. Starlink Mobile has picked Qualcomm to power a land-based 5G network in the US, and the rollout starts in 2027. That matters because AT&T's Mobility segment made 96.9% of its 2025 segment operating income.

So far, customers aren't leaving. Postpaid phone churn was 0.92% in the third quarter of 2026, the same as a year earlier.

AT&T trades at about 9x forward earnings. That's close to its five-year average of 9.2x and below its 12-year average of 11x. Analysts expect normalized EPS to grow about 11% a year, from $2.12 in 2025 to $2.92 in 2028. For the stock to work, those estimates just have to hold.

Analysts have still trimmed their targets. The average fell from $30.61 a year ago to $27.59:

That average, from 24 analysts, is still 24% above today's price.

Key Takeaways

A $400,000 portfolio split evenly across Comcast, Hormel Foods and AT&T pays about $20,500 a year in dividends at today's prices, or about $1,710 a month.

Comcast's dividend is the best covered of the three, taking 24% of its free cash flow over the last twelve months, against 44% for AT&T and 82% for Hormel.

If Hormel, the least covered, halved its dividend, the income would fall to about $17,000 a year. If it stopped paying, the income would fall to about $13,600.

Hormel's dividend still looks safe to me, and its Dec. 3 call, its first since closing the $1.055 billion Brakebush deal, is the next thing to watch.

Any retiree hunting for dividend income will look hard at stocks yielding around 5%. Comcast (CMCSA:NASDAQ), Hormel Foods (HRL:NYSE) and AT&T (T:NYSE) all pay about that today.

So let's take a hypothetical retiree who splits $400,000 evenly among the three. At today's prices, that buys about 5,210 shares of Comcast, about 5,870 of Hormel and about 5,960 of AT&T. Their dividend checks add up to about $20,500 a year, or about $1,710 a month. That's a 5.1% yield on this part of the portfolio. (Of course, no one should ever own just three stocks.)

The checks are about the same size. Each one, though, takes a very different share of its company's free cash flow:

Source: TIKR, at today's prices, with dividends at each company's current annual rate. TTM is the twelve months to each company's latest quarter. Forward is fiscal 2026 consensus.

Comcast has the most room to spare

Comcast's core business is losing customers. It lost 144,000 domestic broadband customers in the third quarter of 2026, against 91,000 a year earlier, as fiber and fixed wireless rivals keep pressing on price.

None of that has strained the dividend. Over the twelve months to Sept. 30, 2026, Comcast paid $4.82 billion in dividends out of $19.66 billion of free cash flow, a very comfortable 24%. Its free cash flow has stayed far above its dividends for a decade:

Comcast (CMCSA): free cash flow vs. common dividends paid, $ billions, fiscal 2016–2025 (TIKR)

Analysts expect less this year. The 16 who estimate it see fiscal 2026 free cash flow 29% below its last reported figure, which lifts the ratio to 36%. That's still well-covered. Comcast is spending on new pricing and free wireless lines, which Co-CEO Michael Cavanagh said on the third-quarter call are "necessary to strengthen customer relationships and position the business for a return to growth over the long term."

title: Is T-Mobile Stock A Real Bargain After Its Slide?
detail:
Is T-Mobile Stock A Real Bargain After Its Slide?
Trefis Team

TMUS
T
VZ
CMCSA
CHTR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock trades at 15.9 times earnings, against 21.5 for the median S&P 500 company. The shares have lost 20.7% over the past twelve months. The price appears to assume that T-Mobile's postpaid growth will not lift its profit. If so, this is a fair price, not a sound carrier on sale. So is the cash behind that discount actually growing?

Free Cash Flow At T-Mobile Is Still Climbing

Yes, so far. T-Mobile produced $17.8 billion of free cash flow in the four quarters ending September 30, 2026. That is up from $13.8 billion in the four quarters before. At the November 17 close, that cash came to 9.9% of the company's market value.

Behind that cash is a business still adding customers. Sales rose 9.3% over the same twelve months, against 8.7% for the median S&P 500 company. In fiscal Q3 2026, management also reported strong postpaid net account additions. For now, T-Mobile's free cash flow is growing faster than its sales.

T-Mobile's Margin Has Slipped Over Twelve Months

T-Mobile's profit has not kept pace with its sales. The carrier posted a 20.7% operating margin over the twelve months ending September 30, 2026, down from 22.6% a year earlier. Operating income stood at $19.4 billion in both periods, so the extra sales added no operating profit. Net income, the profit the P/E is built on, fell to $11.3 billion from $11.9 billion.

Over a longer stretch, T-Mobile is growing faster than it used to while keeping less of each sale. Its latest sales growth beat the 6.2% average of the last three twelve-month periods. But its latest operating margin fell short of its three-period average of 21.5%.

The weakest of the last four quarters was fiscal Q4 2025, at a 15.4% operating margin. The margin was 24.1% in fiscal Q2 2026 and 24.0% in fiscal Q3 2026. The Q3 figure beat the 21.9% of fiscal Q3 2025. Still, two stronger quarters are not yet a recovery.

T-Mobile Expects More Cash, But Owes Heavy Debt

Management has raised its own bar. On the fiscal Q3 2026 call, the company lifted its 2026 forecast for adjusted free cash flow, a measure management defines itself. The new midpoint is $18.8 billion, up from $18.6 billion in July. It also expects postpaid organic service revenue to grow about 7% in fiscal Q4 2026.

Buyers also take on a company whose debt equals 65.7% of its market value. For the S&P 500 taken as one company, the figure is 19.8%. Management said on the same call that more of its capital in 2027 and 2028 will probably go to spectrum auctions. It also puts shareholder returns after spectrum and acquisitions. T-Mobile bought back $10.3 billion of stock in 2026 through October 23. Because those returns rank last, buybacks are what a holder stands to lose if the cash stalls or spectrum takes more of it.

AST SpaceMobile's (NASDAQ:ASTS) stock closed at a record high of $133.09 per share on May 28, 2026. But today, the satellite maker's stock trades at about $29 per share.

Why did AST's stock plummet 78%?

AST produces low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for cellular connectivity. It helps wireless carriers, including AT&T (NYSE:T) and Verizon (NYSE:VZ), expand their networks to remote areas.

AST has already launched 13 of its BlueBird satellites, but it won't generate stable recurring commercial revenue until it launches at least 45 satellites. AST originally planned to reach that milestone by the end of 2026, but it pushed that target back to 2027 earlier this year.

The second major shock was SpaceX's (NASDAQ:SPCX) $8 billion acquisition of Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum. That spectrum, which once belonged to T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS), could turn Starlink into a major wireless carrier.

When would I consider buying AST's stock?

From 2026 to 2028, analysts expect AST's revenue to surge from $166 million to $1.65 billion as it expands its constellation toward its long-term goal of 248 satellites.

They also expect its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) to turn positive at $1.20 billion in the final year. With an enterprise value of $10 billion, AST's stock already trades at seven times that bullish estimate.

Therefore, I wouldn't be surprised if it gets cut in half to the mid-teens in the next market crash. But if that happens, I'd buy some shares as a long-term play on space-based cellular networks.
